name: Pseudoexon Suppression (Pseudoexon Skipping)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Restore normal mRNA splicing by preventing inclusion of a pathogenic pseudoexon generated by a cryptic splice site.
molecularDefect: Deep intronic variants create or strengthen cryptic splice donor/acceptor sites, resulting in inclusion of a pseudoexon that disrupts the coding sequence.
diseaseMechanism: Inclusion of a pseudoexon introduces additional sequence into the mature transcript, frequently causing frameshifts or premature termination codons and subsequent nonsense-mediated decay or production of a dysfunctional protein.
suitableVariantTypes: Deep intronic variants; cryptic splice-site variants; intronic variants causing pseudoexon activation.
typicalDiseases: Stargardt disease (ABCA4); Duchenne muscular dystrophy (selected intronic variants); Cystic fibrosis; Neurofibromatosis type 1; CEP290-associated Leber congenital amaurosis; other inherited disorders caused by pseudoexon activation.
rnaTargetRegion: Activated pseudoexon; cryptic splice donor site; cryptic splice acceptor site; intronic splicing enhancer/silencer elements regulating pseudoexon inclusion.
transcriptRequirement: Presence of a validated disease-causing pseudoexon generated by an intronic mutation.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs; commonly 2′-O-methyl phosphorothioate (2′-OMe PS), PMO and other splice-switching chemistries.
typicalLength: Approximately 18–25 nucleotides (varies by target and chemistry).
designRules: Literature synthesis: mask cryptic splice sites or regulatory elements controlling pseudoexon inclusion; avoid RNase H activation; experimentally verify restoration of normal splicing by RT-PCR.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible intronic regions surrounding the activated pseudoexon are preferred.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential unintended effects on normal alternative splicing; transcriptome-wide splice analysis is recommended.
advantages: Directly corrects deep intronic splicing defects without genome editing; restores physiological splicing; highly mutation-specific.
limitations: Applicable only when a pathogenic pseudoexon has been experimentally identified; highly mutation-specific; repeated administration required.
clinicalTrialExamples: QR-1011 (ABCA4-associated Stargardt disease, investigational); Sepofarsen (CEP290-associated LCA10, investigational); additional inherited retinal disease programs.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic evidence and multiple clinical development programs, but no FDA-approved therapy specifically for pseudoexon suppression.

referencesSummary: Anna & Monika (2018); Chen et al. (2024); Sangermano et al.; Aartsma-Rus et al.
